The Attention Equation: Scaled Dot-Product Attention Explained
description:
The Transformer architecture is the foundation of modern AI, but its true power lies in a single, elegant mathematical operation: Scaled Dot-Product Attention.

In this masterclass, we strip away the abstraction and audit the exact linear algebra that allows LLMs to calculate context in real-time. We break down the transformation of input embeddings into Query, Key, and Value vectors, the $QK^T$ dot-product operation, and the final Softmax normalization that determines model intelligence.

What we cover:

Projection Geometry: How $W_Q, W_K, W_V$ weight matrices define vector spaces.The Attention Score: Deconstructing the $QK^T$ alignment matrix.

Mathematical Stability: Why we scale by $\frac{1}{\sqrt{d_k}}$ to prevent exploding gradients.

Normalization: How Softmax converts raw scores into probability distributions.This video is for builders and students who want to move beyond prompt engineering and understand the actual mechanical engine of deep learning.

#DeepLearning #Transformers #LinearAlgebra #NeuralNexus #AIArchitecture

title: Linear Algebra and Optimization for Machine Learning, Part 1.
description:
The new Springer eBook "Linear Algebra and Optimization for Machine Learning" explains the mathematical foundations of linear algebra and optimization within the context of machine learning in the first 3 Chapters.
Chapter 1: Introduction to Linear Algebra and Optimization
This chapter serves as an introduction to fundamental structures and concepts.
Fundamentals: Scalars, vectors, and matrices are introduced, along with basic operations such as addition, multiplication, and transposition.
Matrix Multiplication: Matrix multiplication is viewed as a decomposable operator that can be interpreted either as a combination of row/column operations (elementary matrices) or as a geometric transformation (rotation, reflection, scaling).
Machine Learning: Initial connections to machine learning are established by introducing classic problems such as classification, regression, clustering, and outlier detection.
Optimization: Concepts such as Taylor expansion (for function simplification) and gradient descent are introduced as tools for training models.
Chapter 2: Linear Transformations and Linear Systems
The focus here lies on the geometry of transformations and the solution of systems of linear equations.
Transformations: Matrix multiplication is defined as a linear map (transformation) capable of preserving properties—such as orthogonality and distances (rigid-body transformations)—or altering them (scaling).
Vector Spaces: Concepts such as subspaces, bases, dimensions, coordinates, and the "span" of a set of vectors are explained in detail.
Systems of Equations: Row echelon form and Gaussian elimination are utilized to solve linear systems and perform matrix inversion.
Optimization Perspective: Solving linear systems is viewed as an optimization problem (least squares), leading to the introduction of the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse and projection matrices. Chapter 3: Eigenvectors and Diagonalizable Matrices
This chapter deepens the analysis of matrices through their decomposition.
Determinants: These are defined both recursively and geometrically as a measure of the change in volume resulting from a transformation.
Diagonalization: The central theme is the computation of eigenvalues ​​and eigenvectors in order to decompose matrices into a simpler form.
Symmetric Matrices: It is demonstrated that symmetric matrices are always orthogonally diagonalizable—a fact that is crucial for applications such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and the covariance matrix.
Quadratic Optimization: The role of matrices (specifically the Hessian matrix) in determining minima, maxima, or saddle points in quadratic functions is examined.
Numerical Algorithms: Finally, methods such as the power method for determining dominant eigenvectors, as well as the Schur decomposition, are introduced.
These chapters form the foundation for subsequently understanding more complex topics—such as the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) or advanced optimization techniques—in detail.

title: Linear Algebra | Lecture 26 (last)
description:
Resumed Determinants, using typeset notes (based on Gowtham Kurri's note). Recalled the axiomatic definition (Definition 1), then stated and proved some properties of the determinant (Lemma 2), using the axioms, showed how the determinant can be deduced for the 2×2 case uniquely, motivated the proof idea (Example 3), skipped Example 4 that does it for 3×3 matrices, stated and proved the result for the general n×n case (Theorem 5: explicitly gives the unique formula for the determinant of an n×n matrix). After this, stated and proved that det(AB)=det(A)det(B) (Proposition 7) using Theorem 5, stated Example 6 without proof for now (left that as an exercise). In the last fifteen minutes or so, introduced the trace (Definition 8), explained how trace and determinant are closely related, e.g. by det(exp⁡(A))=exp⁡(Tr(A)). Explained how inverses are computed using determinants (without proof), showed that A is invertible iff detA≠0 using this (and the fact that the left and right inverses of any square matrix A must be identical), i.e. Lemma 10 and Fact 9. Ended by stating Theorem 13 that shows that trace is the sum of eigenvalues and determinant is the product of eigenvalues. Had to leave the proof as an exercise but showed how det(exp⁡(A))=exp⁡(Tr(A)) can be seen to hold for self-adjoint matrices, using Theorem 13.

Cloud clusters cover a wide range of scales: from the turbulent cloud cluster that we observe in the sky with our naked eyes to the gigantic organized cloud bands such as Monsoons, The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), Cyclones,  the Madden-Julian oscillation (MJO) etc. that satellites observe. On these different scales clouds either aggregate through their own local cloud-circulation feedbacks or sometimes they are seen to ride on top of vortices linked to waves and instabilities. Although the monsoon dynamics has been studied for a long time, how monsoon convection organizes on a variety of time-scales is an unresolved enigma. The program will be organized around this unresolved scientific direction.

The program will tie threads across the three themes:

Geophysical fluid dynamics
Physics of atmospheric convection
Understanding variability in monsoon dynamics

title: The Feedback Revolution: New Tools for Spectral Line Analysis - Sophia Flury
description:
Speaker: Sophia Flury (University of Edinburgh)

Title: The Feedback Revolution: New Tools for Spectral Line Analysis

Abstract: Feedback is perhaps the most crucial phenomenon in shaping the evolution of astrophysical objects, from exoplanets and protoplanetary disks to star clusters, galaxies, and even the Universe itself. In the era of big data, sprawling archives, and deeper than ever spectra, astronomers have pushed up against the limits of what we can learn about feedback from standard methods of analyzing spectral lines. Most standard line flux ratio diagnostic diagrams have not been calibrated on state-of-the-art physics and chemistry, which may be missing critical signatures of feedback. Moreover, kinematic analysis of spectrally resolved lines relies heavily on decades-old methodologies which miss fundamental physics or on expensive forward-modeling of assumption-prone simulations. I will present new tools for learning more about the physics of feedback. As case examples, I will illustrate how exhaustive ionization models can resolve tensions in chemical evolution and how novel line profile models can provide insights into geometry and driving of winds at a fraction of the cost of IFU observations. With these publicly available tools in hand, the community is now poised to revolutionize the study of feedback in a wide variety of contexts.

Cloud clusters cover a wide range of scales: from the turbulent cloud cluster that we observe in the sky with our naked eyes to the gigantic organized cloud bands such as Monsoons, The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), Cyclones,  the Madden-Julian oscillation (MJO) etc. that satellites observe. title: Mars Just Revealed New Clues Of Ancient Life (But Something Is Missing)
description:
For billions of years, Mars has been silent.

No oceans. No movement. No sign that anything ever lived there. From orbit it looks completely dead — a frozen desert that stopped changing long ago.

But recently, NASA's Curiosity rover found something buried inside ancient Martian rock. Not fossils. Not bones. Organic molecules — complex chains of chemistry that on Earth became the building blocks of life. Hidden inside rock billions of years old, preserved from radiation, waiting to be found.
And that discovery changes the question entirely.

Because Mars wasn't always like this. It had rivers. Lakes. An atmosphere thick enough to hold heat and water in place. For millions of years it had everything life needs — water, energy, chemistry, and time. The same ingredients that produced life on Earth.

So why didn't it happen?

That may be the most unsettling question in science right now. Not whether Mars had the right conditions — it did. But why, even with everything in place, life never began. And what that means for every other planet we've ever called habitable.

Here is what we cover in this documentary:
🔴 What Curiosity Actually Found

title: Dr. Dominik Lungerich - Navigating through the Jungle of Ball Milling Parameters
description:
Recent advancements in mechanochemistry are revolutionizing synthesis as a greener and more efficient alternative to solution-based methods, and in addition, enabling reaction pathways that are otherwise inaccessible through classical methods. As a result, its potential has captured the attention of both academia and industry.
However, for researchers coming from a classical solution-based chemistry background, adopting mechanochemistry remains challenging: the kinetics of solution-based chemistry do not fully translate, and the role of its many parameters—especially those tied to milling equipment—remains only partially understood.
This talk will serve as a beginner’s guide to the wide variety of parameters that require attention and introduce tools, such as kinematic models, to improve the reproducibility and predictability of mechanochemistry.

title: The Curiosity rover found molecules on Mars linked to life
description:
Sealed inside a slab of rock on the cold surface of Mars are molecules that scientists are struggling to explain away. NASA's Curiosity rover drilled into an ancient lakebed, baked the powder in a tiny onboard oven, and detected the largest organic molecules ever found on the Red Planet — long chains of carbon that, here on Earth, are tied to the chemistry of life itself. Some of them may be billions of years old.
So is this the biggest discovery in human history? Or just ordinary chemistry on a dead world? That's exactly the tension at the heart of this video. The same molecules that could be the fragments of ancient Martian cell membranes can also form with no life at all, and that maddening ambiguity has split the scientific world in two.
We travel back to a warmer, wetter Mars with rivers and lakes, follow the patient detective work that uncovered these fragile molecules, and confront the history of false alarms that has taught scientists to be so careful. And we arrive at the unsettling truth: the answer to whether we are alone may be locked in rock just a few meters down — rock we cannot yet reach.
Make yourself comfortable, dim the lights, and let yourself be carried to the surface of another world. By the end, you may never look at that small red point of light in the night sky the same way again.
If you enjoy this video, leave a like, subscribe, and tell us in the comments whether you think life ever existed on Mars. It would truly mean a lot to us.

title: Lesson 5 — The Seeking System: The Dopamine Engine of Creativity
description:
Why does discovery feel so good that we chase it even against the odds? Meet the seeking system — the ancient mesolimbic dopamine pathway Jaak Panksepp identified as the brain's great incentive engine. This lesson shows how dopamine rewards not just answers but the hunt itself, why anticipation alone energizes a new project, and how play, passion, and intrinsic motivation amplify it — while deadlines and stress shut it down. How to Create Proteomics, Transcriptomics, or Metabolomics Visualizations With EnrichViz R App
description:
This video explains how to create your proteomics, transcriptomics, or metabolomics pathway analysis visualizations using the R app EnrichViz.
You can use the app directly from website, no installation required: https://rgmilian.shinyapps.io/EnrichViz/ 
Alternatively, you can download the app from the Github: https://github.com/rologmilian/enrichviz
To cite the app: 
Garcia-Milian R, (2026). EnrichViz: Interactive visualization of enriched 
pathways and biological functions from omics data (Version 1.0.9) [Shiny application]. GitHub. https://github.com/rologmilian/enrichviz.git 

Use this blurb for your methods: 
Pathway and functional enrichment results were visualized using EnrichViz  v1.0.9 (Garcia-Milian, 2026), a freely available R Shiny application designed for  interactive, publication-ready visualization of enrichment analysis output  from proteomics and transcriptomics experiments. Enrichment results exported  from [IPA / g:Profiler / Enrichr — specify tool used] were provided to the  application as comma-separated value files alongside a normalized abundance  matrix and a sample annotation file mapping each sample to its experimental 
group.
For each analysis, the top enriched pathways and biological functions were  ranked by significance using -log10(p-value) and displayed as bar plots and  bubble plots, where bubble size represented the number of molecules associated  with each term and colour intensity represented the false discovery rate (-log10(FDR)). Pathway–molecule connectivity was examined using chord diagrams, in which arc width encodes the number of connections and ribbons represent  individual pathway–molecule associations. Z-score normalized expression  patterns for proteins or genes within selected pathways were displayed as  clustered heatmaps, with rows corresponding to individual proteins or genes  and columns to samples ordered by experimental group. The normalized abundance  distribution of individual proteins of interest across experimental groups was  examined using boxplots and violin plots. Group colors were applied  consistently across all visualizations. All figures were exported as PNG files  at 300 dots per inch (dpi) for inclusion in the manuscript.

title: FoodWay - A Smart Food Delivery System Using Data Structures and Algorithms
description:
FoodWay: A Smart Food Delivery System Using Data Structures and Algorithms  
Department of Internet of Things and Robotics Engineering University of Frontier Technology, Bangladesh 

Abstract—
Food delivery applications have become increasingly popular in recent years. However, many existing systems suffer from inefficient route planning and order management. This paper presents FoodWay, a smart Android-based food delivery application that utilizes Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) to improve delivery efficiency. The system incorporates ArrayList, HashMap, Queue, Graph, and Dijkstra’s Algorithm to optimize order processing and route selection. Restaurant FoodWay System Graph Index Terms—Food Delivery, Android Application, Data Structures, Dijkstra Algorithm, Route Optimization I.

OBJECTIVE 
Queue Delivery System The objectives of this project are: 
• Reduce delivery time 
• Improve route optimization 
• Manage customer orders efficiently 
• Implement practical DSA concepts 
• Develop a user-friendly Android application 

II. INTRODUCTION 
Food delivery services have become an essential part of modern life. Customers expect fast and reliable services. Traditional systems often face challenges in route planning, delivery assignment, and order management. FoodWay addresses these issues through efficient implementation of Data Structures and Algorithms. The application provides optimized route selection and organized order processing. 

III. PROBLEM DESCRIPTION 
Existing food delivery systems face several challenges: 
• Slow delivery process 
• Poor route optimization 
• Inefficient order management 
• High waiting time 
• Lack of intelligent delivery assignment These issues negatively affect customer satisfaction and overall system performance. 
IV. SYSTEM DESIGN 
The system consists of the following modules: 
• Customer Module 
• Order Processing Module 
• Payment Module 
• Delivery Module 
• Route Optimization Module Customer 

V. SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE 
VI. APPLICATION FEATURES 
• Food Ordering System 
• Add to Cart 
• Price Calculation 
• Payment System 
• Delivery Tracking 
• User-Friendly Interface 
• Lottie Animation Support 
VII. DSA CONCEPTS USED 
A. ArrayList ArrayList is used to store food items dynamically. 
B. HashMap HashMap is used to map food items with their prices. 
C. Queue Queue is used to process customer orders using FIFO methodology. 
D. Graph Graph represents locations and routes. 
E. Dijkstra Algorithm Dijkstra’s Algorithm is used to determine the shortest delivery route.

VIII. ALGORITHM DESIGN Algorithm Steps: 
1) User selects food items 
2) Store items in ArrayList 
3) Retrieve prices using HashMap 
4) Add order to Queue 
5) Construct Graph 
6) Execute Dijkstra Algorithm 
7) Generate shortest path 
8) Complete payment 
9) Deliver order 

IX. COMPLEXITY ANALYSIS TABLE I: 
Complexity Analysis Operation Complexity 
ArrayList Insert O(1) 
HashMap Search O(1) 
Queue Operation O(1) 
Graph Traversal O(V+E) 
Dijkstra Algorithm O(ElogV ) 

X. RECURRENCE RELATION ANALYSIS 
Order processing can be represented as: 
T(n) = T(n−1)+1 
Solving the recurrence: T(n) = O(n) 
For graph traversal: T(V,E) = O(V +E) 
For shortest path calculation: T(V,E) = O(ElogV) 

XI. APPLICATION SCREENSHOTS 
XII. INPUT AND OUTPUT I
nput: • Burger = 2 • Pizza = 1 • Juice = 1 
Output: • Burger = 300 BDT • Pizza = 250 BDT • Juice = 50 BDT • Total = 600 BDT 
• Payment Successful 
• Order Confirmed 
XIII. TESTING AND VALIDATION 
The application was tested with multiple food orders. The system successfully stored food items, processed orders, calculated total prices, and generated optimized routes.
 (a) Home Screen 
 (b) Restaurant 
 (a) Food Menu
 (b) Add to Cart
Food Ordering Process

XVII. FUTURE WORK 
Future enhancements include: 
• GPS-based live tracking 
• Firebase integration 
• Online payment gateways 
• AI-based route optimization 
• Multi-restaurant support 
• Push notification system 
• User recommendation system 
• Cloud database integration 
• Delivery analytics 
• Cross-platform support  

XIV. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION 
The FoodWay application successfully demonstrates the practical implementation of Data Structures and Algorithms. 

The use of ArrayList improves data management, HashMap enables fast price retrieval, Queue ensures organized order processing, and Dijkstra’s Algorithm optimizes delivery routes. Experimental observations indicate improved efficiency and reduced delivery time.

title: UNIEGO Explained AI That Learns From 9 Different Perspectives | Future of AR Glasses & Egocentric AI
description:
What if an AI could learn not only from what you see, but also from what depth sensors, skeleton trackers, third-person cameras, and multiple expert systems see at the same time?

In this video, we break down UNIEGO, a groundbreaking AI framework designed to solve one of the biggest challenges in egocentric vision: understanding the world from a single first-person wearable camera.

Traditional wearable cameras suffer from limited field of view, self-occlusions, and missing context. UNIEGO tackles this problem by learning from multiple expert teachers during training and then compressing all that knowledge into a single efficient model that only needs one camera during deployment.

We'll explore:

• Why standard knowledge distillation fails
• The representational gap problem
• Conflicting gradients between multiple AI teachers
• Proxy Learning (Level-I Distillation)
• Proxy Merging Initialization
• Selective Proxy Distillation (SPD)
• How UNIEGO learns from depth, skeletons, and third-person views
• State-of-the-art results on EgoExo-Fitness, Assembly101, and EgoExo4D
• Why this matters for AR glasses, robotics, and future AI assistants

One of the most fascinating aspects of UNIEGO is that it gains the wisdom of multiple sensors and viewpoints during training but requires only a single egocentric camera at inference time. This makes it highly practical for next-generation wearable AI systems.

If you're interested in Artificial Intelligence, Computer Vision, AR Glasses, Robotics, Multimodal AI, Machine Learning Research, and the future of Human-AI interaction, this paper is definitely worth understanding.

Watch till the end to see how UNIEGO achieves state-of-the-art performance while remaining lightweight enough for real-world deployment.

title: What AI & Machine Learning Actually Are (And Aren't) | Cut Through the Hype
description:
Artificial Intelligence is everywhere.

Every week brings new headlines promising revolutionary breakthroughs, job replacement, superintelligence, and unlimited possibilities. But beneath the hype lies a much more practical and useful reality. Many business leaders, developers, product managers, and decision-makers still misunderstand what AI actually is, leading to poor investments, failed projects, and missed opportunities.

In this episode of Master AI/ML, we cut through the noise and explain what Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning really mean, how they relate to one another, what powers modern AI systems, and the myths that continue to confuse organizations around the world.

🚀 In This Episode

✅ AI vs Machine Learning vs Deep Learning

✅ Why these terms are not interchangeable

✅ How machine learning learns from data

✅ Why deep learning transformed modern AI

✅ The most common AI myths

✅ Why AI doesn't actually "think" like humans

✅ AI hallucinations and why they happen

✅ Data quality versus data quantity

✅ Will AI replace all jobs?

✅ Why you don't need a PhD to use AI

✅ The three ingredients behind every AI system

✅ Data, Math, and Compute Power

✅ What AI can do well

✅ What AI cannot do

🤖 The Big Three Explained

Artificial Intelligence is the broadest category.

Machine Learning is a subset of AI that learns patterns from data.

Deep Learning is a subset of Machine Learning that uses layered neural networks and powers many of today's most impressive AI systems.
Understanding how these technologies fit together is one of the most important foundations of AI literacy.

💡 Myth Busting

This episode tackles some of the most dangerous misconceptions about AI:

❌ AI thinks like a human

❌ AI is always right

❌ More data automatically means better AI

❌ AI will replace every job

❌ You need a PhD to use AI

We'll explain why each of these beliefs is misleading and what professionals should understand instead.
⚙️ What Actually Drives AI?

Every modern AI system ultimately depends on three ingredients:

📊 Data

📐 Math

💻 Compute Power

Understanding these foundations helps explain why some AI projects succeed while others fail.

🎯 Key Takeaway

AI is neither magic nor science fiction.

It is a powerful set of technologies built on data, mathematics, algorithms, and computing power. The more clearly you understand its strengths and limitations, the better decisions you'll make about products, investments, careers, and innovation.

The goal isn't to fear AI or worship AI.

The goal is to understand it.

title: How Is an AI Actually Trained? (Explained in 6 Simple Steps) 🤖
description:
Ever wonder how an AI like ChatGPT actually learns to talk? It's not magic — it's six steps. This quick, friendly animation breaks down how a Large Language Model (LLM) goes from a giant pile of raw text to something you can chat with.

Here's the whole journey: 
1️⃣ Gather + clean the data — feed it a huge chunk of the internet, then filter out the junk 
2️⃣ Break text into tokens — every word becomes a number 
3️⃣ Pretraining — it plays "guess the next word" billions of times until it gets good 
4️⃣ Instruction tuning — show it great examples so it answers like an assistant 
5️⃣ Human feedback — people pick the better answer to teach it manners 
6️⃣ Test + ship it — check that it's helpful, honest, safe & fast, then launch

No jargon, no math degree required. Perfect if you're curious about AI but want the big picture in plain language.

👉 Which step surprised you most? Let me know in the comments.

description:
Your Sock Drawer Just Explained KNN

Ever wondered how AI makes a decision when it has never seen something before?

K-Nearest Neighbors, or KNN, is one of the simplest machine learning ideas: look at the closest examples, see what most of them are, and make a decision from the crowd.

In this example, a mystery sock does not know where it belongs. So it checks the nearest socks around it. If most nearby socks are blue, it probably belongs with the blue pile. That is KNN in plain English.

Simple idea. Powerful result.

title: Why ChatGPT Gives Different Answers (Decoding Explained) #GenerativeAI #LLM #MachineLearning #AI
description:
Ever wonder why ChatGPT gives a different answer when you hit "regenerate"? The secret is decoding — and most people have never heard of it.

Here's the surprise: a language model never actually outputs a word. At each step it produces a raw score (a "logit") for every token in its vocabulary — often 100,000+ of them. Something then has to choose just one. That choice is decoding, and it's the single biggest dial between safe, repetitive answers and creative, surprising ones.

In this 6-minute explainer I break down, in plain language:
→ How logits become probabilities (softmax)
→ Greedy vs sampling
→ What temperature, top-k and top-p (nucleus) actually do
→ Why generation is a loop (autoregression)
→ A real OpenAI API call + the math in ~10 lines of numpy
→ Which settings to use when (temp 0 for code, ~0.7 for chat, higher for brainstorming)

The rule of thumb that saves you headaches: tune temperature OR top-p — not both. And for reasoning models, just leave the defaults locked.

Once you see it, you'll notice this one quiet slider behind every AI reply you read.

What temperature do you use day-to-day? 👇

title: ​Trash to Treasure gone wrong! 😱 #diy #tech
description:
I found an old, discarded Lapcare USB hub with a broken cable while digging through some junk. Instead of throwing it away, I decided to open it up, solder a new USB cable onto the board, and try to bring it back to life!

Thank you everyone for your support! This video and the one I made with MKBHD were big projects for me but it's a fascinating subject and I learned so much making it. I have a Masters degree in Computer Engineering but feel like I learned more making this than I did after 4 years of University! Processors really are remarkable and visualising them as accurately as I could was such a wonderful journey. As I say at the end of my video, I hope I got some of that wonder across. 
 
 
📖 INTRODUCTION TO THE HIDDEN CITY INSIDE YOUR PHONE:
 
There's another world inside your phone, a beautiful city of  mind-boggling, time-stopping power and yet it's a mystery to almost everyone. Not because it's hard to understand, it's not, but because it's hard to see and harder still to visit. This book, like the video on which it's based, is a journey into one of the wonders of the world, in a way that nobody has experienced before.  
 
Before I wrote this book, my phone felt incredibly practical but not very special, It was an expensive but very useful brick. I never spent time thinking about how it actually did all the wonderful things it did . The irony is I have a Masters degree in computer engineering, where I spent years learning about the very thing that explains how processors, the tiny electronic brains inside our phones, actually work. Despite this, I still took its helpfulness and power for granted.
 
In this respect, phones remind me a bit of airplanes, technical marvels that we mostly underappreciate. So much so that we can sit inside a 400 tonne metal tube, miles from the ground, whisking us to another part of the planet at incredible speeds and we're focused on whether we should order beef or chicken to arrive on a tiny tray. Humans are very good at normalising the almost impossible until it's mundane. But there is a key difference between a plane and a phone, we can see planes at work. Not when we're inside them, complaining about the legroom, but when we stand on firm ground and look at the sky. And there they are, almost beyond belief, steel birds of wonder, carrying hundreds of people through the clouds. That's when we see what technology can actually do, technology can be magical. We can't have that moment with a tiny processor hidden inside a phone because we can't see it fly. So it remains… a useful brick. But what if you could go inside? And what if the skies inside your phone were perforated with a glittering copper city, on an atomic sea of barely imaginable size? What if the processors inside our useful bricks, games consoles, computers and more that run the modern world, were actually simple to understand but live in a completely different world and time from us? 
 
If there was a chance that one of the greatest wonders of the modern world was in your pocket right now, wouldn't you want to know how that was possible? I'm here to tell you it is and I'm going to do my very best to take you on a journey there so you can see and experience it for yourself. 
 
As with the companion video on my Epic Spaceman YouTube channel, this will be a simple, accessible journey, full of images rather than numbers, for people of any background and age.
 
And it's time this journey began…

title: S. Dipierro: The (fractional) Malmheden Theorem
description:
Date: Friday, 19 June, 2026 - 10:00 to 11:00 CEST
Title : The (fractional) Malmheden Theorem
Speaker: Serena Dipierro, University of Western Australia

Hosted at: SISSA, International School of Advanced Studies, Trieste, Italy
Organizers : Pavan Pranjivan Mehta** and Arran Fernandez*** 
** SISSA, International School of Advanced Studies, Italy
*** Eastern Mediterranean University, Northern Cyprus

Keywords: Mean Value Theorem, Malmheden Theorem, fractional Laplacian

Abstract

We present a classical result by Malmheden based on a simple algorithm to determine the harmonic function in a ball, and we discuss the fractional counterpart, from which one obtains a representation formula for s-harmonic functions as a linear superposition of weighted classical harmonic functions and a new simple proof of the fractional Harnack inequality.

Biography

Serena Dipierro took her PhD in Mathematical Analysis at the International School for Advanced Studies (SISSA, Trieste) in 2012. After PostDoc positions at the Universidad de Chile and University of Edinburgh, and a Humboldt Fellowship, she held permanent positions at the University of Melbourne and the Università di Milano. In August 2018 she moved at the University of Western Australia, where she is now Professor of Mathematics.

Serena is Fellow of the Australian Mathematical Society, and Australian Mathematical Society Hanna  Neumann Lecturer. She has obtained prestigious awards, including the Australian Mathematical Society Medal, the Mahony-Neumann-Room Prize, the Bartolozzi Prize of the Italian Mathematical Union, the  Christopher Heyde Medal of the Australian Academy of Science, and the Prize of the Bulletin of the Brazilian Mathematical Society.

Bibliography

[1] Dipierro, Serena; Valdinoci, Enrico, Elliptic partial differential equations from an elementary viewpoint - a fresh glance at the classical theory. World Scientific Publishing Co. Pte. Ltd., Hackensack, NJ, (2024) xvii+651 pp.
[2] Bucur, Claudia; Dipierro, Serena; Valdinoci, Enrico, On the mean value property of fractional harmonic functions. Nonlinear Anal. 201 (2020), 112112, 25 pp.

title: Data-Driven Discovery and Verification of Singularities in Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations
description:
Motivated by the Clay Prize problem on the blowup of Navier-Stokes equations (NSE), I present numerical approaches that facilitate deeper insights into singularity formation, demonstrating that machine learning methods, especially Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Neural Operators, significantly enhance the capability to identify and characterize potential blowups with high precision. Motivated by an exact symbolic search for blowups, we pioneered the Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN) architecture, a novel machine learning paradigm whose interpretability and excellent scaling properties are achieved through learnable nonlinearities, gaining broad recognition in the AI for science community.

Building on these insights, I introduced a robust analytical framework to establish blowups with clear stability, with rates automatically inferred, and without explicit spectral information of the linearized operator. This formulation naturally suggests a robust numerical algorithm for tracking singularity formation and beyond, potentially applicable to singularities with multiple scales and complicated systems like NSE. Finally, I will talk about our resolution of a longstanding open problem of non-uniqueness of weak solutions to NSE, which is crucial in the understanding of turbulence, leveraging again the synergy between high-fidelity numerical solutions and rigorous computer-assisted proofs.

Speaker Bio: Yixuan Wang is a PhD candidate in applied math at Caltech. His research builds systematic proofs inspired by numerics and amenable to computer-assisted verification, alongside high-precision machine learning tools such as neural operators and pioneered the Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN), particularly motivated by the study of the Navier-Stokes singularity, one of the Millennium prize problems.

title: Unlocking Nature's Secrets: The Power of Reverse Differential Equations
description:
Welcome to Science Hub! Today, we're diving into an exciting advancement in the world of differential equations that could revolutionize how we understand natural phenomena. Scientists have long relied on differential equations to model and predict everything from weather patterns to the behavior of cells. But now, the spotlight is on inverse partial differential equations, which work in reverse to unveil hidden causes from observed data. This reverse engineering is crucial for uncovering the mysteries of chromatin structure within cells, a key player in gene interaction and regulation. 

However, the challenge lies in predicting changes in chromatin amidst noisy and complex data. Enter 'smoothed layers', a groundbreaking technique that's simplifying this complexity. While high-powered computing has been the go-to solution for tackling scientific problems, recent research shows that smarter mathematical methods can be even more effective. Smoothed layers reduce computational complexity and data noise, enhancing the ability of artificial intelligence to identify intricate patterns. 

This innovative approach is proving particularly promising in genetic research, offering fresh insights into cellular gene regulation. Chromatin, a complex structure within the nucleus, critically influences gene activity, affecting everything from cell identity to function. Thanks to smoothed layers, scientists can now track gene interactions over time, paving the way for new treatments for genetic diseases like cancer and aging. 

But the potential of this technique extends beyond genetics. It's applicable in fields such as fluid dynamics and materials research, where complex differential equations are used. By providing a more stable and efficient means of uncovering hidden factors in various scientific systems, smoothed layers could transform our understanding of the laws governing them. 

Developed by a team at the University of Pennsylvania, this method offers an innovative solution to the challenges faced by scientists in inverse differential equations. By refining fundamental mathematics instead of relying solely on brute computational force, this technique could spark a revolution across scientific fields, from gene organization insights to improved weather predictions. This new approach might just unlock future discoveries that significantly impact science and technology. 

Stay curious, and don't forget to subscribe to Science Hub for more fascinating science stories!

title: Temporal API Crash Course (JavaScript’s Biggest Upgrade)
description:
JavaScript’s biggest ES2026 feature is Temporal — a modern replacement for the old Date object.

The current Date API has been painful for decades: weak timezone handling, surprising mutation, inconsistent parsing, and runtime differences. Temporal starts fresh with clear, separate types for each date/time concept:

✅ PlainDate — date only (no time, no timezone)
✅ PlainTime — time only (no date, no timezone)
✅ ZonedDateTime — date + time + explicit timezone
✅ Instant — one absolute moment on the global timeline
✅ Duration — a span of time for arithmetic

Best part: everything is immutable and parsing is consistent — basically the API Date should’ve been from the beginning.

If you’ve struggled with dates/timezones in JavaScript, Temporal is the upgrade you’ve been waiting for.

Timeline / Chapters
0:00 Temporal replaces Date (ES2026 headline)
0:20 Why the current Date API is painful

title: SQL Server Architecture Explained: Protocol Layer, Relational Engine & Storage Engine
description:
🚀 Understanding SQL Server Architecture is the foundation for becoming a skilled DBA or database developer. In this video, we break down the core components that make Microsoft SQL Server work—from the moment a client sends a query to when the results are returned.

🔍 What You'll Learn:
✅ Client-Server Architecture – How SQL Server communicates with clients [citation:1]
✅ Protocol Layer – Shared Memory, TCP/IP, Named Pipes & TDS (Tabular Data Stream) [citation:6]
✅ Relational Engine (Query Processor) – CMD Parser, Optimizer & Query Executor [citation:6]
✅ Storage Engine – Data storage, file types (.mdf, .ndf, .ldf), Buffer Manager & Transaction Manager [citation:1]
✅ SQLOS (SQL Operating System) – Memory management, scheduling & thread synchronization [citation:1]
✅ Query Lifecycle – From T-SQL to execution plan to data retrieval

📚 Who This Is For:
- SQL Server Beginners
- Database Administrators (DBAs)
- Developers working with SQL Server
- Anyone preparing for SQL Server certification


💡 Key Takeaway: SQL Server architecture follows a three-component model: Protocol Layer ➡️ Relational Engine ➡️ Storage Engine [citation:6]. Understanding each layer helps you write better queries, troubleshoot performance issues, and design efficient databases.

title: Advanced use of CASE + COUNT in [SQL]
description: Learn how to streamline complex SQL queries by integrating `CASE` statements directly within aggregate functions like `COUNT` and `SUM`. This powerful technique eliminates the need for multiple filtered queries and cumbersome `GROUP BY` clauses, allowing you to generate multi-column reports for different categories in a single, efficient pass. By understanding how aggregate functions handle null values versus zeros, you can craft elegant one-liners that perform high-speed data analysis and significantly level up your database management skills.

title: The hack of COUNT Function in SQL
description: Mastering the distinction between different counting methods in SQL is a fundamental skill that can prevent common data analysis errors. This lesson clarifies a frequent point of confusion by demonstrating how one command retrieves the total number of rows in a table regardless of their content, while another specifically targets non-null values within a chosen column. By understanding whether your query is simply counting every row or evaluating individual entries for actual data, you will gain the necessary foundation to use more advanced logic and ensure your database reporting is always accurate.

title: The CASE Expression in SQL
description: The CASE expression is a versatile SQL tool that allows you to transform raw numerical data and codes into meaningful labels and categories using intuitive if-then-else logic. By evaluating conditions from top to bottom and returning a value as soon as the first match is found, it provides a powerful way to classify records—such as sorting customers into premium, standard, or basic tiers based on their lifetime value. Mastering this technique is essential for presenting polished, business-ready results, though it requires careful sequencing of conditions to ensure the most restrictive criteria are met first.

title: GitLab Tutorial: Importing Third-Party Security Vulnerability Reports
description:
Streamline your security posture and automate vulnerability remediation by integrating third-party security scanners with GitLab via native SARIF support. In this technical walkthrough, Fernando Diaz, Developer Advocate at GitLab, demonstrates how the platform ingests, validates, and acts upon standardized security logs directly within your continuous integration pipelines. You will learn how to enable automated Static Application Security Testing (SAST) features, analyze comprehensive vulnerability reports, and implement auto-generated code fixes to continuously protect your delivery cycle.

Fernando covers the step-by-step configurations needed to activate SAST false positive detection and vulnerability resolution workflows across your group settings. Using a real-world project example, you will see how an open-source scanner like Semgrep dynamically flags critical security flaws and converts that telemetry into actionable code fixes inside a merge request interface. The demo highlights how GitLab applies rigorous development guardrails, including custom approval policies, to block insecure commits from reaching your production environment before code ever hits a branch.

Key Topics:

description:
Git authentication issues happen when the remote can't verify who you are, an expired SSH key, a bad or lapsed access token, or pushing over HTTPS when a token is required instead of a password. The fix is to refresh and re-register the credential. Essential for the CompTIA AutoOps+ exam.

title: Detached HEAD Short for Exam Prep | AutoOps+ Git Troubleshooting #comptia
description:
Detached HEAD means you checked out a specific commit instead of a branch, so HEAD points at the commit directly. New commits here belong to no branch and are easy to lose. Fix it by creating a branch with git switch -c, or just check out a branch again. Essential for the CompTIA AutoOps+ exam.

title: Ethernet Shared Media 🔥 Explained Simply
description:
Ethernet Shared Media is a networking concept where multiple devices share the same communication medium to transmit data. In traditional Ethernet networks using hubs, all connected devices compete for bandwidth, which can lead to collisions and reduced performance. In this video, we explain how shared media works, collision domains, CSMA/CD, and the evolution from shared Ethernet to modern switched networks. Perfect for CCNA students, networking beginners, and IT professionals.

title: 1G vs 10G SFP+ Uplink Explained in 10 Seconds! 🤯 #itinfrastructure  #networkingpower
description:
Are you bottlenecking your entire network architecture with a single cable? Watch this 3D visual comparison of a 1G Copper Uplink vs. a 10G SFP+ Fiber Massive Capacity flow!

In this video, we break down a common critical mistake in enterprise networking: connecting a 24-port switch to the core network using only a standard 1G RJ45 patch cable.

🔍 The Math Behind the Bottleneck:
If all 24 ports on your Gigabit switch are pushing data at maximum capacity, you have 24Gbps of traffic trying to squeeze through a 1Gbps uplink. This creates a massive 24:1 oversubscription ratio! The result? Severe network congestion, physical data packet drops, and sky-high latency.

🚀 The 10G SFP+ Solution:
By upgrading your uplink to a 10G SFP+ optical transceiver and using fiber optic cables, you expand your bandwidth pipeline by 10x. The data streams merge seamlessly, ensuring frictionless, hyper-fast, and perfectly organized data transmission—like a high-speed hyperloop for your packets!

Don't let your uplink be the weak link. Whether you are running a server room, upgrading an enterprise network, or building a high-end homelab, your hardware deserves the right connection.

title: The Rise of On Device AI Agents Explained | Rakesh Gohel
description:
The Rise of On Device AI Agents Explained | Rakesh Gohel

Every cloud API call has a cost, a latency, and a privacy risk. 

Local AI is solving all three at once..

This is not a prediction. It is already happening.

Google's Gemma 4 family runs full agentic, multimodal AI on a standard 16GB laptop. No cloud. No API bill. No data leaving your device.

And this week they pushed it further.

DiffusionGemma released recently, it generates entire text blocks at once instead of word by word. Up to 4x faster inference. On hardware you already own.

But Google is not building this alone.

📌 Here is what the major AI companies are shipping:

1. Google Gemma 4 + DiffusionGemma

- Runs full agentic and multimodal tasks on a 16GB laptop
- DiffusionGemma generates entire text blocks at once, not token by token
- Delivers up to 4x faster inference on local hardware

2. Microsoft Phi-4

- Trained on curated, high-quality data rather than raw web crawls
- Achieves graduate-level reasoning while running locally on consumer hardware

3. Meta Llama 3.2

- 1B and 3B models built specifically for on-device deployment
- Full model fits in 650MB RAM and runs on most smartphones

4. Alibaba Qwen 2.5

- Handles 29 languages locally without a single external API call
- Performs on par with models 10x its size on domain-specific tasks

📌 So where does this leave AI architecture decisions?

Cloud AI remains the right choice for large-scale reasoning, high-volume enterprise workloads, and centralized governance.

Local AI is the right choice for latency-sensitive tasks, privacy-first workflows, offline environments, and cost-sensitive deployments.

Hybrid AI is where most production systems will eventually land.

The architecture question is no longer only: "Which model API should I use?"

It is now: "Where should this intelligence actually run?"

That is a more important question than most organizations are asking today.

The real shift is not from big models to small models. It is from renting intelligence to owning it.

💰 The Spanish Gold That Bankrupted an Empire!
In the 16th century, Spain struck unimaginable wealth — fleets loaded with gold and silver poured in from the New World. Overnight, Spain became the richest nation on Earth… but that fortune soon turned into a curse. Without realizing it, they had unleashed the first wave of global inflation. In this episode of History of Money (#8), discover how boundless treasure led to economic collapse, endless wars, and repeated bankruptcies. Learn the powerful lesson Spain taught the world: true wealth isn’t what you own — it’s what you create.

title: 80 Years Since The Atomic Bombing Of Hiroshima & Nagasaki
description:
80 Years Since The Atomic Bombing of Hiroshima & Nagasaki is a powerful historical documentary that examines the missions that introduced the world to the nuclear weapon. On August 6, 1945, the Enola Gay dropped the uranium-based Little Boy on Hiroshima. Three days later, on August 9, 1945, Bockscar delivered the plutonium-based Fat Man to Nagasaki. The atomic bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki changed the course of World War II and marked the first, and only use of a nuclear weapon in war.

This film uses a combination of authentic archival footage and stunning 3D animations created in Unreal Engine to recreate the atomic bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki with historical accuracy and cinematic impact. Viewers will see the missions unfold from takeoff to detonation, experiencing the unprecedented destructive power of the nuclear weapon.

The atomic bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki revealed the devastating effects of a nuclear weapon, from the fireball and blast wave to the radiation that followed. These events reshaped global politics, ignited the nuclear arms race, and forever altered the debate on the role of the nuclear weapon in warfare and deterrence.

Eighty years later, the legacy of the atomic bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki continues to influence nuclear weapon policy and disarmament efforts. This documentary blends history, technology and science to tell the story of the nuclear weapon’s first combat use and reflects on the lessons of the nuclear age.

Experience history, technology, and the reality of the nuclear weapon in this unforgettable film.

title: Indian History Like Never Before | Ancient Civilizations to Independence
description:
Indian History Like Never Before | Ancient Civilizations to Independence
#indianhistory   #ancientindia  #historydocumentary 

Step into the timeless journey of one of the world’s oldest and most vibrant civilizations in "Indian History Like Never Before | Ancient Civilizations to Independence" — a powerful, in-depth documentary that uncovers the full arc of India’s rich historical legacy.

From the urban planning marvels of the Indus Valley Civilization, one of humanity’s earliest known societies, to the philosophical depth of the Vedic Age, India has long stood as a cradle of culture, knowledge, and innovation. This film explores the rise of Jainism and Buddhism, two revolutionary movements that reshaped the spiritual world not just in India, but across Asia.

We trace the political and cultural brilliance of the Maurya Empire, with Emperor Ashoka’s dramatic transformation from conqueror to peace-loving ruler, and the Gupta Empire, often called the “Golden Age” of Indian art, science, and literature. Discover the enduring legacies of South India’s powerful dynasties like the Cholas, whose naval dominance extended Indian influence as far as Southeast Asia.

As the documentary progresses, we delve into India’s medieval period, including the era of the Delhi Sultanate and the opulent reign of the Mughal Empire, known for architectural marvels like the Taj Mahal and cultural fusion between Persian and Indian traditions.

We then explore the arrival of European colonial powers, especially the British, and how India transformed under foreign rule. Witness the rise of resistance — from the 1857 Revolt to the Indian National Congress, and from the non-violent movement led by Mahatma Gandhi to the firebrand nationalism of Subhas Chandra Bose.

This documentary brings to life the personal sacrifices, the mass mobilizations, and the dreams that fueled India’s freedom struggle, culminating in the Partition of 1947 and the creation of modern India and Pakistan.

But the story doesn’t end there. We also examine Independent India’s journey — the drafting of its secular, democratic constitution under Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the leadership of Jawaharlal Nehru, the Green Revolution, economic challenges, and the liberalization of the 1990s that catapulted India into a new global era.

Through stunning visuals, compelling narration, and well-researched storytelling, this film is a perfect educational and inspirational resource for students, educators, history lovers, and global citizens seeking to understand India not as a collection of events, but as a living civilization with a past that continues to shape the future.

👉 Don’t forget to like, share, and subscribe for more deep-dive documentaries on world history, civilizations, and untold stories.

title: The Full Biography of Cleopatra | Documentary
description:
Who was the real Cleopatra beyond the Hollywood myths? What did the last queen of Egypt actually look like? And where is her long-lost tomb? This documentary follows archaeologist Kathleen Martinez on her passionate 15-year quest to solve one of history's greatest mysteries.

Was Cleopatra truly the seductress that Roman propaganda painted her to be? Archaeological evidence reveals a brilliant strategist who spoke nine languages and ruled Egypt for 21 years. How did Cleopatra manage to captivate both Julius Caesar and Mark Antony, Rome's most powerful men? And what really happened in Cleopatras final days, as she faced defeat by Octavian?

From the sunken ruins of ancient Alexandria to the mysterious tunnels beneath Taposiris Magna, new discoveries are challenging everything we thought we knew about Cleopatra. Did she really die by the bite of an asp? Why did she choose to be worshipped as the goddess Isis? And could her tomb, filled with unimaginable treasures, be hidden in an ancient temple just outside Alexandria?

Join us as archaeologists uncover unprecedented evidence - from golden coins bearing her true image to ancient offering tables that might lead to Cleopatras final resting place. After 2,000 years, the search for history's most famous queen continues.

title: Japan & India  A Perfect Economic Match Explained
description:
At first glance, Japan and India may seem very different. One is a highly developed technological powerhouse with an aging population, while the other is a rapidly growing economy with a young workforce. Yet these differences are exactly what make them such strong economic partners.

Japan possesses advanced technology, capital, manufacturing expertise, and decades of industrial experience. India offers a vast consumer market, abundant talent, growing infrastructure needs, and one of the world's largest labor forces. Together, they complement each other's strengths and help offset each other's challenges.

Japanese investments have supported major Indian projects, including transportation networks, industrial corridors, logistics systems, and manufacturing facilities. In return, Japanese companies gain access to a fast-growing market and an alternative production base as global supply chains diversify.

Beyond economics, both nations share strategic interests. They support a stable Indo-Pacific region, secure trade routes, and stronger economic cooperation across Asia. This alignment makes their partnership about more than profits—it is also about long-term regional stability and growth.

The reason many analysts view Japan and India as a natural economic match is simple: Japan has capital and technology, while India has scale and growth potential. When these strengths combine, both countries stand to benefit, creating a partnership that could shape Asia's economic future for decades to come.

title: Introduction - Sophimatics: Integrating Philosophy, Logic, and AI for Computational Wisdom
description:
The provided text, excerpts from "Sophimatics: Integrating Philosophy, Logic, and AI for Computational Wisdom" by Gerardo Iovane and Giovanni Iovane, introduces Sophimatics, a novel concept aimed at advancing artificial intelligence beyond current limitations. It proposes that modern generative AI, despite its proficiency in pattern recognition, lacks genuine understanding, intentionality, purpose, context, and a grasp of time. Sophimatics seeks to address these deficiencies by integrating philosophical principles—such as dynamic ontology, intentionality, and dialectical reasoning—with computational architectures and complex temporal modeling. The authors contend that this interdisciplinary approach, combining philosophy, logic, and computational science, can lead to more ethical, context-aware, and interpretive AI systems capable of reflective dialogue and deeper understanding. The work primarily lays out the theoretical framework for this "computational wisdom," with practical implementation reserved for future studies.

Defining Computation: We start by precisely defining what constitutes a computer and how this relates to the mind.

title: #11 Pipes and the Unix Philosophy - Introduction to Linux Command Line
description:
In this video, we explore pipes in Linux — one of the most powerful ideas in the Unix world.
Pipes allow you to take the output of one program and feed it directly as input to the next. This lets you chain simple commands together to perform more complex tasks, all from the command line.

We start with a quick recap of input/output redirection, then move into:

How pipes work in Bash

Treating programs as filters

Combining commands to build processing pipelines

The Unix philosophy: small programs that do one thing well
Sending stdout only, stderr only, or both through pipelines
Using tools like cat, sort, uniq, tr, and aspell together
How to clean and normalize text using pipelines
How process substitution allows piping only stderr
By the end of the video, you’ll understand how to create powerful command chains that transform data step by step — the way Unix was designed to be used.

👉 In the next video, we’ll explore essential filters like grep, wc, head, tail, sort, and more.

title: Introduction to The Philosophy of History — G. W. F. Hegel | Full Audiobook (Public Domain)
description:
Begin Hegel’s most accessible gateway into his grand vision of world history. In the Introduction to The Philosophy of History, Hegel argues that Reason governs the world, that history is the unfolding of human freedom, and that great events are driven by world-historical individuals and the spirit (Geist) of an age. Clear, forceful, and provocative, this introduction frames the famous survey of Oriental, Greek, Roman, and Germanic worlds by asking: What is history for? and How do we find meaning in it?

What you’ll hear

Reason in history and the march of freedom

The state, civil society, and morality

Nations, “world-spirits,” and great leaders

Hegel’s method: dialectic, necessity vs. contingency

Author: G. W. F. Hegel (1770–1831)
Work: Introduction to The Philosophy of History (public domain translation)
Audio: Public domain | For study & reference

If you’re exploring philosophy, political theory, or the meaning of historical progress, this is a classic starting point—perfect for students and lifelong learners.

title: The Philosophy of Physics, with Elise Crull
description:
What happens when physics meets the big questions of philosophy? Neil deGrasse Tyson and comic co-host Chuck Nice sit down with Elise Crull, philosopher of physics at CUNY and author of The Einstein Paradox, to explore physics, philosophy, and how thought experiments shape real science. 

Why did 20th-century physicists like Einstein, Schrödinger, and Bohr disagree about what quantum mechanics even means? Why did Einstein insist that physics needed deeper explanations, and how did philosophical thinking guide his breakthroughs? Was he really doing physics—or philosophy? And what does it mean to “do” science when the evidence runs thin?

From Newton’s Principia to quantum entanglement, we explore how physics and philosophy were once deeply intertwined—and why that relationship matters now more than ever. Why did physics and philosophy split in the first place? What do we lose when science becomes only experimental and utilitarian?  Is there still room in modern physics for “why” questions? Plus, we debate whether scientists can truly leave their worldview at the lab door?

How did Newton and Einstein’s philosophies differ? We explore philosophical differences between great scientists and how it yielded different results. What philosophical leap helped Schrödinger and others imagine the electron as a wave? We break down if today’s physicists still need philosophy to address unanswered quantum questions. What does “entanglement” really mean? Could echoes of the early universe’s quantum state still be hiding in the cosmos? If science is a method, who decides which questions matter? And what happens when the data runs out… but the questions remain?

title: 12th Prof. R L Kapur Oration Lecture 2026 by Dr. Ajit V. Bhide
description:
12th Prof. R L Kapur Oration Lecture on “Mirror, Mirror, On the Wall, I’m the Loneliest of Them All” by Dr. Ajit V. Bhide
Date:  Friday, June 12, 2026 | Time: 4  PM  
Venue: JRD Tata Auditorium, NIAS.

Abstract: Fragile Connections in the Modern World In recent times, two phenomena of human psychology appear to have reached epidemic proportions. Loneliness is increasingly experienced in life, in various ranges of age. It seems ironic that this attends on so many lives in an era when communication has become easily accessible and rapid. Another partly related spectacle is an increasing preoccupation with one self. It would be fair to state that the age of Narcissus is upon us. The presentation will focus on these two aspects of modern mental life with insights into their causation and the possibility of healing.

Speaker: Dr. Ajit V. Bhide completed his education entirely in Bangalore. He joined St Martha’s Hospital, Bangalore, in 1987 and led its Department of Psychiatry from 1996 to 2021; he now serves as Emeritus Consultant. His work spans youth mental health, family and social dimensions of psychiatry, anxiety and personality disorders, psychotherapy, ethics, and preventive psychiatry. As President of the Indian Psychiatric Society, he played a key role in advancing the decriminalisation of homosexuality, with the Society’s position cited by the Supreme Court of India, and in shaping ethical guidelines on professional boundaries later adopted by the Medical Council of India. A widely engaged contributor to professional bodies, he has chaired and advised numerous committees. Beyond medicine, he is an avid reader with deep interests in literature, Indian history, and music, and has  active in theatre and film, including award-winning productions.

title: Erich Fromm Lecture 2025 | Discussion
channelName: Erich Fromm Study Center Berlin - EFSC
description:
Public Psychoanalysis for today: Why Erich Fromm matters

The Erich Fromm Study Center hosts the annual Erich Fromm Lecture at the IPU Berlin. This year's speaker is Prof. Neil McLaughlin, Professor in the Department of Sociology at McMaster University (Canada).

This presentation will tell the story of Fromm's public psychoanalytic career and discuss how public psychoanalytic life has been transformed by new technology and our polarized politics. We will conclude by making the case that the example of Fromm's public intellectual work is a more valuable model to build on than contemporary public psychosocial thinkers such as Jordan Peterson, Gabor Mate and Avgi Saketopoulou.

title: The Brain Glitch That Bends Time #neuroscience #psychology #brainhacks
description:
We ask a complex question: if the brain constructs reality in real-time, could it accidentally reconstruct another time? This science explainer dives into how the human brain doesn't passively record the world but actively predicts it. Discover the fascinating concept of predictive processing and how it relates to our perception, including phenomena like time distortion. 🧠✨
We ask a dangerous question: if the brain constructs reality in real time, could it reconstruct another time? This video explores how the human brain predicts rather than passively records the world, a core concept in neuroscience explained through predictive processing. Understanding this process helps clarify how our perception and reality are formed, and how phenomena like time distortion can occur. Join us for an engaging neuroscience lecture on cognitive science and the brain's incredible capabilities. 🧠🔬

title: Inaugural Lecture of PD Dr Sandra Andraszewicz
description:
In her talk celebrating her Venia Legendi (habilitation), Sandra shares key insights from over a decade of her research at the ETH Zurich, Switzerland, at the Singapore-ETH Centre, Singapore, and her collaborations including her alma mater - the University of Basel. She guides the audience through the meaning of complexity in decision-making. She explains how the complexity of the decision problem, human individual differences and the social and physical environment influence decision processes and outcomes. She explains how human physiology, bodily and brain processes manifest during decision-making. Taking innovation and digitalisation in the spotlight, she shows how technology augments psychological phenomena and what this means for financial regulators, policy-makers and product and service providers. She covers topics such as:
- social media,
- digital payments,
- cryptocurrency use and adoption,
- digital engagement practices in online applications,
- reaching sustainability goals,
- resilience,

and psychological concepts as:
- social influence,
- technology adoption,
- personality,
- cognitive biases,
- cognitive modelling.

Lecture date: 26.02.2026

title: UEA Lasdun Lecture - Why We Watch: The psychology of reality and the power of story
description:
Stephen Lambert (SOC78), one of Britain’s most successful television producers and a UEA graduate, will explore what lies behind our fascination with reality and competition shows, from The Traitors and Undercover Boss to Race Across the World and Squid Game: The Challenge. Drawing on his experience creating global hits watched by millions, he will reflect on how the best unscripted storytelling taps into universal human instincts – trust and betrayal, empathy and ambition, fear and hope – to reveal who we are and how we behave under pressure. 
In this lecture, Lambert will examine the psychology of why we watch, and why we care so deeply about ‘real’ people in extraordinary situations. His talk will be followed by a conversation with a UEA academic about storytelling, human nature and the evolution of television in the streaming age.

description:
Welcome to DP CORE, a psychology-focused YouTube channel created to help you understand the human mind, take the right moves in life, and grow with clarity and confidence. This channel is designed primarily for a United States–based audience, and all content is delivered in clear, fluent English so that psychology feels practical, relatable, and useful in everyday life.

DP CORE exists for one reason: better thinking leads to better decisions, and better decisions lead to a better life. In a world full of distractions, misinformation, and emotional pressure, understanding psychology is no longer optional—it is essential. DP CORE helps you develop that understanding step by step.


---

What DP CORE Represents

The name DP CORE stands for the core principles of decision psychology. At the heart of everything we create is the belief that most life problems are not caused by lack of intelligence, but by lack of awareness.

People struggle not because they are weak, but because:

They don’t understand how emotions influence logic

They underestimate the power of habits

They fall into common psychological traps

They react instead of responding


DP CORE helps you identify these patterns and correct them using psychological insight, not motivation alone.


---

What You Will Learn on DP CORE

DP CORE focuses on applied psychology—psychology that improves real life, not just knowledge. We break down complex concepts into simple explanations so you can apply them immediately.

Topics covered on DP CORE include:

title: Dana Chisnell and Christian Crumlish on the DOGE-ification of Civic Design
description:
Dana Chisnell and Christian Crumlish on the DOGE-ification of Civic Design


When Dana Chisnell and Christian Crumlish took roles in U.S. federal agencies, they knew the work wouldn’t be easy. But what unfolded during their time under the second Trump administration went far beyond bureaucratic resistance. In this gripping conversation, they recount the painful dismantling of teams like 18F and the Department of Homeland Security’s Customer Experience Office—takedowns that were less about efficiency and service, and more about ideology and erasure. From executive orders scrubbing DEI language to gutting digital service teams and exfiltrating government data, they describe what it felt like to navigate a coordinated unraveling of public-serving infrastructure.



Yet out of the ashes, a new civic design seeds are taking root. Christian and Dana reflect on what it means to build systems that endure, how to design for accountability, and where the next generation of mission-driven designers, researchers, and creators might focus their efforts. There’s urgency here, but also a throughline of resolve and resilience: the belief that better government is possible—and that good people are still fighting for it.









What You'll Learn from this Episode:

     
     
  •  How design and research teams inside U.S. government agencies were dismantled under political pressure
     
     
  •  The tactics used to erase DEI and disability-facing efforts and language from federal operations
     
     
  •  Why civic tech and design teams need to plan for resilience—even under hostile leadership
     
     
  •  What it looks like to “exfiltrate” ethical infrastructure during a transition of power
     
     
  •  How former public servants are reshaping the civic tech ecosystem post–government
     
     
  •  Why designing for accountability matters as much as designing for access

title: “Could you make it worse?” Redesigning HealthCare.gov
description:
A self-described “failed architect,” Sha Hwang joins Lou to discuss the challenges of scale when merging two companies, and his journey from Trulia and Stamen Design to being part of the team that rescued Healthcare.gov and, subsequently, founding Nava, a public benefit corporation formed during those efforts.

About Sha’s talk, The Lost Year: The pandemic made it painfully clear that the failure of critical public services causes real harm, both physical and financial. Our healthcare system is being overwhelmed, millions are pouring onto unemployment, and we’ve seen an unprecedented number of people trying to access government programs. It has never been more important for government services to be simple, effective, and accessible to all, yet we’re far from that vision today. In this talk, Sha Hwang, co-founder and chief operating officer of Nava Public Benefit Corporation, will discuss the opportunities designers have to build government services that prioritize equity and resiliency—and the responsibility that comes with designing systems that serve millions of people.

About Sha:
Sha Hwang is the COO and co-founder of Nava, a public benefit corporation formed during efforts to help fix HealthCare.gov. Nava partners with government agencies to improve critical public services, and now works across several projects in the US on programs including Medicare, Veterans Affairs, and unemployment benefits and paid family leave at the state level. Nava has helped tens of millions of people enroll in critical programs, streamlined processes to save decades of labor years, and saved government agencies hundreds of millions of dollars. A failed architect and accidental entrepreneur, Sha has worked with clients such as the New York Times, the Harvard Library Lab, MTV, Flickr, and Adobe. Previously, Sha worked at Stamen Design and later cofounded the company Movity, which was acquired by Trulia.

Real World Civic Data & Analytics in Baltimore City Government
Does Baltimore City government even know how to use data? Why is [insert service here] still paper-based? Where are the hotspots for illegal dumping? Is President Trump right about the rats?

Smart cities, civic data use, and urban data analytics are all hot topics, but what are the current capabilities and applications in our own city government? With his previous organization, Navigant Consulting, Justin supported the U.S. Department of Energy’s appliance standards program – the unsung hero of the Obama administration’s climate change efforts – through analysis and developing Federal regulations. He also used data science to improve utility energy efficiency programs.

Justin holds an M.S. in mechanical engineering from Columbia University, where he researched applied data science in the energy sector and was a National Science Foundation fellow in the “Integrative Graduate Education and Research Traineeship”, with a program focus of “Solving Urbanization Challenges by Design”. title: Present Continuous Tense: Rules, Examples & Common Mistakes 🚀
description:
English Grammar Lesson: Master the Present Continuous Tense!
Kya aapko English bolte waqt tenses mein confusion hoti hai? Aaj hum seekhenge Present Continuous Tense — ek aisi tense jo hum un actions ke liye use karte hain jo abhi is waqt ho rahe hain.
Is video/post mein hum cover karenge:
✅ Pehchaan (Identity): Raha hai, Rahi hai, Rahe hain.
✅ Formula: Subject + is/am/are + Verb(1st Form) + ing + Object.
✅ Daily Life Examples: "I am learning English", "She is eating food."
✅ Negative & Interrogative Sentences: Kaise sawaal poochein aur mana karein.

While the global narrative of generative music often centers on Western pioneers, the Indian subcontinent possesses deep-rooted foundations in procedural art and indigenous musical theory. This keynote moves beyond standard industry frameworks to explore how traditional Indian musical structures can be bridged with modern computational logic.

Through live-coding performance platforms and the history of their development, I will demonstrate how programming functions as a performance art that intentionally blurs the line between engineering and creative expression. The address will examine the process of "creatively decolonizing" technology by adapting Western-developed systems to better represent diverse cultural contexts and microtonal complexities.

A central focus of this session is pushing back against the inherent technological biases found in standard audio software. We will discuss the technologist's vital role in reclaiming computational heritage and creating sustainable futures for non-Western musicality. Ultimately, this keynote serves as a call for the audio developer community to evolve into ""creative technologists"" who lead the way in building an inclusive and egalitarian global ecosystem.

title: SUNO New STEM Separation TOOL is FIRE! 🔥🔥🔥 #mastering #mixing #engineering #music
description:
🎵 STEM SEPARATION MASTERCLASS (Basics)
What Is Stem Separation?
Stem Separation (also called Source Separation or Audio Source Separation) is the process of taking a finished song and splitting it into individual parts:
• 🎤 Vocals
• 🥁 Drums
• 🎸 Guitar
• 🎹 Piano / Keys
• 🎸 Bass
Think of it like this: You have a baked cake with flour, sugar, eggs, and butter all mixed together. Stem separation tries to pull those ingredients back out. Not easy — that’s why early results were messy.
What Is a Stem?
A stem is a group of related tracks mixed together (e.g., Vocal Stem, Drum Stem, Guitar Stem). Mixing engineers have used them for decades.
Why Use Stems?
• 🎤 Karaoke — Remove vocals
• 🎸 Practice — Isolate or remove an instrument
• 🎹 Remixing — Rearrange parts creatively
• 🎧 Mixing — Import into your DAW (Logic, Ableton, FL Studio, etc.) and tweak individually
Traditional vs AI Separation
Old method: Frequency analysis (pitch, timbre, stereo position). Often caused bleed, artifacts, and muddy results.
AI method: Understands and reconstructs instruments. Much cleaner (e.g., SUNO Advanced Split).
Three Levels
Level 1: Vocals + Instrumental Level 2: Vocals + Drums + Bass + Other Level 3: Granular (Kick, Snare, Acoustic Guitar, Electric Guitar, Synth, etc.)
The Real Goal
Regain creative control. Turn one locked song into separate building blocks you can remix, practice with, or rebuild however you want. 🎤🥁🎸🎹

title: PitchGrid - A Two Dimensional Extension of Western Music Theory
description:
What if the circle of fifths isn't really a circle? This 75-second visual explainer reveals the hidden second dimension in Western music theory.

Starting from the piano keyboard and circle of fifths, we open the circle into the spiral it really is — unfolding it into a line of fifths. Lining up notes in a two-dimensional grid reveals that scales are zigzag patterns (large steps in one direction, small steps in the other), off-scale notes have natural positions, and tuning — from Pythagorean to meantone — becomes a simple knob turn.

title: Financial Basics from the White Coat Investor w/ Dr. James Dahle | BackTable Urology Podcast Ep. 34
description:
Special guest The White Coat Investor James M. Dahle talks with Christopher Beck about where physicians can start when it comes to financial literacy, including common financial mistakes docs make when start practicing, a primer on mortgage rates, and tips on insurance.

---

CHECK OUT OUR SPONSOR

DI4MDs
https://www.di4mds.com

---

SHOW NOTES

In this episode, White Coat Investor founder Dr. James Dahle and our host Dr. Chris Beck discuss strategies for physicians seeking to manage their personal finances and gain financial freedom.
 
First, Dr. Dahle explains the reasoning behind the famous quote, “live like a resident.” He explains that for an early career physician, their greatest wealth-building tool is their income. The income jump from residency to attending years can be extremely useful for quickly paying off student loans. Then, he moves on to discuss another way to resolve student debt, the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) program. This option is ideal for physicians who have spent a significant amount of time working for a nonprofit institution (for example, during training and in academic medicine).

Dr. Dahle advises all physicians to reflect on their priorities when deciding where to allocate their assets. Possible categories could include retirement funds, 529 college savings funds, payment of high-interest debt, and emergency funds. We talk about the power of having a written plan to stay on track with financial goals and prevent ourselves from making rash decisions. 

Next, we discuss different financial vehicles that can provide benefits for physicians. The “back door Roth IRA” strategy allows for yearly contributions to a tax-free retirement fund, even when a physician’s income exceeds the maximum limit for the conventional Roth IRA. Additionally, the funds in a Health Savings Account (HSA) can be used for investment, and then withdrawn at a later date, penalty-free. Dr. Dahle explains the difference between fixed rate and variable rate mortgages, noting that the latter is better for short-term loans because interest rates are unlikely to dramatically increase from year to year. Finally, Dr. Dahle covers the advantages of buying disability insurance as a way to protect physician income, especially for those working in  procedural specialties.

SHOW NOTES

In this episode, White Coat Investor founder Dr. James Dahle and our host Dr. Chris Beck discuss strategies for physicians seeking to manage their personal finances and gain financial freedom.
 
First, Dr. Dahle explains the reasoning behind the famous quote, “live like a resident.” He explains that for an early career physician, their greatest wealth-building tool is their income. The income jump from residency to attending years can be extremely useful for quickly paying off student loans. Then, he moves on to discuss another way to resolve student debt, the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) program. This option is ideal for physicians who have spent a significant amount of time working for a nonprofit institution (for example, during training and in academic medicine).

Dr. Dahle advises all physicians to reflect on their priorities when deciding where to allocate their assets. Possible categories could include retirement funds, 529 college savings funds, payment of high-interest debt, and emergency funds. We talk about the power of having a written plan to stay on track with financial goals and prevent ourselves from making rash decisions. 

Next, we discuss different financial vehicles that can provide benefits for physicians. The “back door Roth IRA” strategy allows for yearly contributions to a tax-free retirement fund, even when a physician’s income exceeds the maximum limit for the conventional Roth IRA. Additionally, the funds in a Health Savings Account (HSA) can be used for investment, and then withdrawn at a later date, penalty-free. Dr. Dahle explains the difference between fixed rate and variable rate mortgages, noting that the latter is better for short-term loans because interest rates are unlikely to dramatically increase from year to year. Finally, Dr. Dahle covers the advantages of buying disability insurance as a way to protect physician income, especially for those working in  procedural specialties.
